feature: A color keeps its place, one layer picked or several
summary: Every color the picked layers have now lives in one Color section that is always there. Shift-clicking a second layer widens what a row speaks for and moves nothing, where before the color you were editing jumped out of the Rectangle, Text or Frame section into a Color section that only existed over a multi-selection.
setup: Photonz Dev, Experiments window, release Next. Nothing to switch on: the Color section is there with saved styles off too, it just loses its styles button.

try.do: Start a blank canvas from the welcome card.
Press R and drag out two boxes side by side.
Press V and click the first box. The Color section holds Fill and Outline.
Shift-click the second box. The same section, the same two rows, the same words.
Click the Fill swatch and pick a color. Both boxes take it, and one undo puts both back.
Untick the Fill checkbox. Both boxes lose their inside and the Fill row stays put, which is the way back.
Press T, click below the boxes, type a word, press V, then shift-click a box. Fill, Outline and Text, all three under Color.
Press F, drag out a frame, click it, and untick its Fill checkbox. That is what No background used to be.

evaluate: Going from one box to two, did your eye stay on the Fill row, or did you still have to re-find it?

A row is now named after the kind of color and never after what is picked: an arrow's color says Outline where it used to say Color, and a frame's surface says Fill where it used to say Background. Does one steady word beat the more exact one?
A highlight's color is called Outline too, which is the weakest case for that word. Does it read wrong enough to want a different one for that whole row?

Between one layer and two, the Color section itself slides about 175 points down the dock, because Align arrives above it and Position & Size grows its multi-layer note. Is that far enough to be annoying, or does the section keeping its name and its rows carry it?
The Fill checkbox now sets a whole selection at once. Does ticking it on three boxes at a time feel safe, given each box comes back with its own outline color rather than one shared one?
A picked highlight brings no settings section at all now, because a color was all it had. Does the dock look emptier than it should, or right?
rough: The screenshots are real captures of the running app, taken by the probe build with Screen Recording granted.

The Color section keeps its name and its rows, but it does not hold still on the screen: about 175 points of drop between one layer and two, all of it from Align appearing and Position & Size gaining a line. Making it truly stationary means putting Color above Align and Position & Size, which is a bigger call about what the dock leads with, so it is a question above rather than a change.

The color well for a single layer is now the app's own picker instead of the system color panel: it lands a color when you pick one rather than on every drag tick, which is one undo step instead of twenty, but it is a different picker than the rest of macOS opens.
A frame's surface lost its own popover, which had a No background button in it. The checkbox does the same job in one click, but there is no longer a place that says the words no background.

A measurement's colors are not in the Color section: they are still inside the Measurement section, because they are not one of the layer color slots. Pick a measurement and a box together and only the box's colors show.
The Effects and Shadow sections still vanish over a multi-selection, so the color problem is fixed and the same problem one section down is not.
